item.title: Reward Shaping for Discovery: A Wordle Case Study
item.description: Fine-tuning a language model with RLVR is known to sharpen it — the policy concentrates on known solutions, boosting pass@1 while pass@k collapses (Yue et al., 2025; Zhao et al., 2025). This is increasingly treated as a fundamental property of RL on language models. But it shouldn’t be. Sharpening is what happens when binary rewards provide zero gradient on problems the model can’t already solve — the capability frontier never moves because the optimization has nothing to push against.

item.title: Process Rewards: An Overview and Outlook
item.description:
1. Introduction

Enhancing LLMs in complex domains requiring multi-step reasoning, logical consistency, and adherence to procedural constraints remains a critical research challenge. Process Reward Models (PRMs) offer the promise to address some of these limitations by providing fine-grained supervision signals throughout the model’s generation process, both at inference and training. They offer denser credit assignment than Outcome Reward Models (ORMs), but are hard to annotate and often ambiguous since characteristics of a good process vary by domain and difficulty of the problem at hand.
